Soil sounds like it should be fine. One last suggestion - humidity! Are you running a furnace or something that might be drying out the air? Less than 40% RH or so and you might want to add a humidifier. I keep one of those combination digital temperature/RH meters next to my plants. You really cant add too much humidity for the plants, but be careful of mold and stuff by making sure to always have airflow.

Constantly filling a humidifier tank is a chore tho, so maybe put it on a timer to only run every few hours or something. Keep an eye on the humidity meter thruout the days and figure out how long the humidity takes to dissipate and what works best for you.

It takes a bit of work to build a properly controlled environment that your plants will flower and fruit in, especially if it's cold and inhospitable outside. Don't stop experimenting tho! you'll get it and it's pretty satisfying when you do. You just need to be able to recreate the environment they thrive in in the warm summer.

Yea humidity is weird - I'm in a northern climate and it's pretty cold right now. It currently says the humidity outdoors is >85% yet inside w/ my furnace running it's about 25%. But the RH percentage is just a percentage of moisture in the air relative to the air being completely saturated, and the amount of moisture a given volume of air can absorb before being completely saturated increases as the temp increases. So if you have 1 cubic foot of air at 30F it might only contain 0.2 ounces of water, yet that is 100% humidity. If you warmed that same volume up to 90F, the 0.2 ounces of water contained by it would only put it at 20%RH - it could contain nearly 1.0 ounces before being at 100%. So I'd recommend getting a humidity meter and seeing what your inside RH is like.
